steps.text: In a large mixing bowl, beat the eggs. Add the milk, brown sugar and nutmeg; stir well to combine.
Soak bread slices in the egg mixture until saturated.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium high heat. Brown slices on both sides, sprinkle with cinnamon and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: French Toast II
raw_recipe.description: A simple French toast recipe that anyone can make. Use your favorite type of bread and serve with your favorite syrup.

review.reviewBody: My husband, who has very little cooking experience, wanted to make french toast for us and so I looked up this recipe for him. This turned out so well that it is now our very favorite recipe for french toast...and I have tried dozens of different recipes for french toast. :)

I think it was delicious. I added 1 teaspoon of vanilla and used brioche. The sugar burned a little, so I cooked it longer over lower heat (a 4 on my gas stove) with a lid. I'm not sure if it burned because I used a non-stick pan. Maybe you'd get different results from a stainless steel or cast iron pan. I'd defer to an expert to know the difference. I'd make it again. Stir the batter between dipping the bread. The spices sink to the bottom.

If you are having trouble getting your french toast to cook all the way through: If you are making a large batch turn your oven to 350 and put them on a foil lined baking sheet AFTER you have cooked them in the pan/griddle. By the time you are ready to start serving you will have fully cooked french toast. If you are making a small batch (i.e for one or two); you can always pop these into the toaster (after they have been cooked through in a pan/griddle) if you think they need to be cooked a little more. On a side note: these freeze and reheat well in the toaster and leave your kitchen smelling wonderful. Also if you know you don't like nutmeg, or you are cooking for a "picky eater" cut back on the nutmeg! .....I add vanilla to this recipe because well I put vanilla in just about everything. Overall a great recipe easy to customize after you make it the first time. (i've always mixed the cinnamon in with the egg even though it gets a little clumpy but if you mix well and swirl it before you dip the bread it makes a lovely dark swirl on the bread). -Happy baking!

Excellent recipe! My new favorite French toast recipe. I made a couple changes to the recipe based on previous reviews. I used 3 eggs, 1/2 cup of milk, 1 TBSP of orange extract, 1 tsp of vanilla extract, 1/4 tsp. nutmeg. I also excluded the brown sugar...which was a mistake, but it turned out phenominal with just the perfect amount of sweetness. I greased the griddle with Crisco and fried the batter dipped, thick french bread slices until golden brown. After cooking, I added a dollop of butter and sprinkled cinnamon and powdered sugar, maple syrup and a small bit of whip cream on the side like the picture above. Perfection!!!

Thank you! This will be in my permanent "wow" them file.

Just made this for family brunch with just a couple of modifications due to what I had on hand. I don’t care much for nutmeg, so left that out and added the cinnamon in with the egg mixture. I used half milk and half liquid vanilla caramel coffee creamer. I put about a teaspoon of vanilla in also. I think the brown sugar in this recipe makes all the difference in the taste. My husband even said my French toast was better than what he makes...that’s a miracle!!

This recipe is great though I tweaked it a bit by using Texas toast, adding the cinnamon to the mixture versus sprinkling it on at the end, and adding a little vanilla extract as well. It cooks up beautifully and tastes great with the right amount of spice!

This is just a simple recipe, and simple sometimes is best!
If your family is fussy, leave out the nutmeg. Here is a note...
....Nutmeg contains small amounts of a drug called myristicin, which is chemically similar to mescaline, the active compound in peyote, and may be converted in the body to one of the related amphetamine-like psychedelics.
Now back to the recipe....I let the slices of white bread "dry out" overnight so the bread is dry to the touch and it won't soak up as much egg mixture & get soggy or fall apart when picking it up out of the bowl. This also speeds up the cooking time since there is not as much egg to cook "in the bread"
(A additional hint is to just use Cinnamon/Sugar mixture instead of adding brown sugar) Also for Diabetics use Spenda/Cinnamon mixture you can make right at home.
Jim B.

Made this, for my husband, two sons and a friend. Came out to 9 slices of Texas Toast. Only thing I did different was add the cinnamon to the egg batter, cause I was lazy about sprinkling on finished toasts. The out come was delish!

Am going to use my recipe of French Toast. Same ingredients, but I like to dip each slice of bread in flour, shake extra flour off, then dip in egg mix. Toast comes out, not soggy at all!

I think this was a good, basic french toast recipe. I only wanted to do 10 slices of bread, which was good because I had no mixture left at all after the 10th slice. To combat the sogginess of the toast, I dried the bread out in the over on 200 degrees for about 10 or 15 minutes, flipping them periodically. I could have left them out overnight to achieve the same results if I had planned ahead. I added a teaspoon of vanilla to the mixture, and sprinkled the finished product with powered sugar and cinnamon. I found I didn't need much maple syrup because the toast has good flavor all on its own.

An easy, quick recipe with great flavor. Have made this twice. The second I was out of nutmeg so just a tad more cinnamon and vanilla extract, the family loved it! The bread used was Pepperidge Farm Farmh9use Hearty White, which quickly and easily soaked up the mix. I was able to get 9 pieces soaking up every bit of the mixture. A define keeper that will be part of breakfast every week.

I used bakery bread, which I left set for several days sliced it fairly thick. I had one slice soak too long, so the rest i pretty much dipped quickly. Added some vanilla to the batter and it was awesome !!!!!!!
Made a nice dinner.
I added more eggs (2) and a tad bit more milk 1/4 cup than stated to make sure all pieces were soaked evenly
Used brioche bread. Tasty.
Delicious.
The French Toast was pretty good. My nephew said it was kinda bland. Maybe make sure you put a touch extra cinnamon as topping. Maybe i didnt sprinkle enough on.
Looking for a simple french toast recipe as my husband or I hadn't made it in years. I found the recipe and he made it. Turned out wonderful.

Second time using this recipe - turned out great again. I used a black cast iron frying pan with a small amount of butter instead of a griddle as we don't have one. The spices really help the toast to not taste "eggy."
I was worried about the 1tablespoon of cinnamon. I will cut down some as it was very cinnamon. I was out of milk so used evaporated milk. I did not soak the bread. I also used wheat bread.

This was a huge hit with my kids and it was super easy for me as someone who is just getting started at making stuff from scratch at home. These had just the right amount of flavor without being too strong. Very easy recipe for a beginner or kids who want to be helpful and have fun in the kitchen.
